President Trump returns to the battleground state of Georgia today for his second rally
in eight days there.
Raul Bali with member station WABE in Atlanta reports the focus is on the state's competitive
U.S. Senate race and open governor's race.
More than 1.6 million Georgians or more than 20 percent of active voters have already cast
ballots.
A Republican nominee for governor Rick Jackson who's running to replace term-limited Governor
Brian Kemp race concerns this week about turnout in Republican-heavy rural Georgia.
The hope is Trump's rallies will help with that.
Jackson is running against Democrat former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms.
The other major race involves U.S. Senator John Ossoff, the only Democratic senator up
for re-election this year in a state won by Trump in 2024.
He's running against Republican Congressman Mike Collins.
For NPR News, I'm Raul Bali in Atlanta.
And former President Obama will be in Ohio and Michigan today.
The U.S. Postal Service says it's taking extra steps starting today to make sure mail-in
ballots for the midterm elections are delivered on time.
NPR's Hansi Lo Wang has more.
The U.S. Postal Service is directing its letter carriers and mail processing plants to pay
extra close attention to mail-in ballots starting today.
It's part of what USPS calls its "extraordinary measures" for speeding up deliveries for
every federal general election.
NPR asked if any post offices are choosing to take any optional measures, like extending
opening and closing times, but USPS did not directly respond.
Its required directives are starting more than a month after the Supreme Court blocked
the Trump administration from using USPS to carry out mail-in voting restrictions for
the midterms.
Many voting advocates are still concerned about last-minute voters getting their ballots rejected.
If your ballot must be received by your local election office by election day, USPS recommends
mailing it back by this Tuesday, October 27.
Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News.
In France, tens of thousands of police have been deployed around the country as authorities
hope to prevent a repeat of the violence that hit the country last weekend.
This has demonstrators protest the rising cost of living and the condition of schools.
Chris Elinor Beardsley is out among one leg of the protests.
Those are some young people chanting "tax the rich!"
I am out in this second big protest march, and it is massive.
I mean, it has filled the entire street.
It's just a human river coursing down this boulevard.
People are angry.
These are not students alone any longer.
You've got people of all ages, middle-aged, older people, and they have rights about how
everything is going in France.
They're screaming, "Everybody hates the police right now!"
And here's Elinor Beardsley reporting from Paris.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
The Kenya Red Cross says that 31 people are reported missing and one person was rescued
following the collapse of a building under construction yesterday in the capital of the
country.
Michael Koloki has more from Nairobi.
According to police, the building located in Nairobi's bustling Isli neighborhood had
more than 10 floors under construction when it collapsed.
Meanwhile, the Kenya Red Cross says search and rescue operations are underway, adding
that a couple of people injured in the incident had been taken to hospital for treatment and
that a tracing center had been set up at the site of the collapse to assist families who
were trying to track down their loved ones.
Building collapses are common in Kenya.
After eight buildings collapsed and killed 15 people in the East African nation in 2015,
a government audit found that over half of the buildings in the country's capital were
unfit for habitation.
For NPR News, I'm Michael Koloki in Nairobi.
As automated vehicles, and that includes robo-taxis, are becoming more common on streets around
the country, some transit systems are thinking about running their trains without humans at
the controls.
That includes Washington, D.C., and also Los Angeles, which plans to run a new automated
track through the Santa Monica Mountains.
Honolulu already operates a driverless train system.
Supporters say it could enhance safety and efficiency.
Game 2 of the World Series takes place in Milwaukee tonight.
The Brewers took Game 1 yesterday with a 3-2 win over the Tampa Bay Rays.
I'm Janine Herbst, and you're listening to NPR News from Washington.
